docTitle: 4 design questions before you make personal records searchable

slides.title:
Ghana made
marriages
searchable
by _name._
slides.sub: 4 design questions it raises for any public registry, from an HCI researcher living in Estonia.

rows.head: Launched August 2026
rows.sub: A public app to search and verify marriages, divorces and licensed marriage officers in Ghana.

rows.head: Four official sources
rows.sub: Registrar-General’s Department, courts, local assemblies, the Ghana Gazette.

rows.head: Records back to 1886
rows.sub: Divorce records, as reported by Ghanamma.

rows.head: Search isn’t proof
rows.sub: Records are still being added. An empty search doesn’t prove someone is unmarried.

slides.title:
Public record.
Now one search
*away.*

rows.a: Someone who knows where to look
A trip to the right office

slides.takeaway: Same record. Far more people can reach it.

slides.title:
Answer yes or no,
not the whole
*history.*
slides.q: Is this person free to marry?
slides.takeaway: Data minimisation: the answer carries only what the question needs.

slides.title:
Who sees
*how much?*
slides.takeaway: Decide which organisations get the fuller view, and why, before anyone searches.

slides.title:
Does a record
mean the same
thing *everywhere?*
slides.note: “It’s not just a privacy engineering conversation. It’s also a cultural design thing.”

cols.v: A divorce record can be just administrative.
Divorce still carries stigma, especially for women.

slides.title:
Can people see
who looked them *up?*
slides.head: Imagined access log
slides.takeaway: In Estonia, I can see what happens to my data in the system. A registry could show people who looked them up.

rows.head: Return the smallest answer.
rows.sub: “Active marriage on record”. No spouse, no dates.

rows.head: Set access levels.
rows.sub: Individuals see status, approved organisations see more.

rows.head: Check what it means locally.
rows.sub: How does a divorce record land for a woman here?

rows.head: Show people who looked.
rows.sub: A log of every search on your name.

slides.title:
Which question
would you _add?_
slides.body: I want more African countries building infrastructure like this, and questioning it while we do.
